tulpa

Bayesian hierarchical models for grouped, spatial and temporal data

tulpa fits Bayesian hierarchical models in R, including models for counts, proportions, repeated measurements, and observations distributed across space or time.

A formula describes how measured predictors and unobserved effects contribute to the response. The engine combines these effects with an observation distribution and fits the model using nested Laplace approximation or Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). Its numerical routines are written in templated C++. The result includes posterior estimates, uncertainty intervals, and diagnostics that help you assess the fit.

tulpa supports:

  • Grouped effects. Random intercepts and slopes, including uncertainty in their variances and correlations.
  • Smooth, spatial and temporal structure. Smooth covariate effects, spatial fields, temporal processes, and combinations of these structures.
  • Several inference methods. Deterministic approximations, MCMC sampling, and correction methods are selected through the same fitting function.
  • Custom models. Model-specific observation likelihoods and custom latent processes are supplied through R or C++ interfaces.

Calibration shows how to assess posterior calibration through repeated simulations. Reliability diagnostics explains what can be checked on an individual fit. The package is experimental and its interface may change.

Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("tulpa")

CRAN provides binaries for Windows and macOS, which need no build tools.

The development version compiles C++17 code. Install the build tools for your operating system first:

Operating system Build tools
Windows Rtools matching your R version
macOS Run xcode-select --install in Terminal
Debian / Ubuntu Install r-base-dev

Check that R can find the compiler:

pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)

Then install tulpa from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/tulpa")

The build links against the BLAS and LAPACK libraries that R itself uses for matrix operations, so no other system library is needed. Package dependencies, including tulpaMesh for spatial mesh construction, are installed with tulpa.

Optional: multithreading

OpenMP lets the nested-Laplace fitters use several CPU threads through n_threads in their control list. The single-process and joint-model reference pages describe the available controls.

Rtools on Windows and the default compiler on Linux include OpenMP. Without it, the package installs and runs on one thread.

macOS setup

Apple’s compiler needs an additional OpenMP runtime. Install it in Terminal:

brew install libomp

Before installing tulpa from source, add the settings for your Mac to ~/.R/Makevars, R’s personal compiler-settings file. Create the directory and file if needed.

Apple Silicon:

CPPFLAGS += -I/opt/homebrew/opt/libomp/include -Xclang -fopenmp
LDFLAGS += -L/opt/homebrew/opt/libomp/lib -lomp

Intel:

CPPFLAGS += -I/usr/local/opt/libomp/include -Xclang -fopenmp
LDFLAGS += -L/usr/local/opt/libomp/lib -lomp

Usage

  1. Fit a model with tulpa().
  2. Inspect the estimates and inference method with summary().
  3. Extract the group effects with ranef().

The built-in InsectSprays data contain insect counts and the spray treatment used for each observation. This Poisson model gives each treatment a random intercept, estimating its effect relative to the overall log count.

library(tulpa)

fit <- tulpa(
  count ~ (1 | spray),
  data = InsectSprays,
  family = "poisson"
)
summary(fit)
effects <- ranef(fit)
Treatment Estimate Lower Upper
spray[A] 0.74 -0.02 1.48
spray[B] 0.79 0.00 1.53
spray[C] -1.14 -1.96 -0.34
spray[D] -0.33 -1.11 0.43
spray[E] -0.67 -1.48 0.10
spray[F] 0.87 0.10 1.61

Supply a data frame with the response, predictors, and grouping variables named in the formula. Choose an observation family appropriate to the response. Data formatting covers response encodings, grouping variables, and spatial inputs.

Random effects, smoothers, and fields

Formula terms describe the model structure. (1 | group) adds random intercepts, (1 + x | group) adds correlated random intercepts and slopes, and s(x) adds a smooth covariate effect. Spatial and temporal specifications describe dependence between locations or times.

Random slopes and covariances walks through inference for group-level variances and correlations. The spatial and temporal articles show how to supply the corresponding structures.

Inference and diagnostics

Automatic mode selects an inference method and records its reason on the fit. An explicit mode selects MCMC, Laplace approximation, or variational inference; variational methods require an explicit choice. Inference modes describes the methods and the models each supports.

Diagnostics depend on how the posterior was computed. MCMC fits report chain convergence and effective sample sizes. Approximation fits report the available integration and inner-approximation checks. Reliability diagnostics explains how to interpret these results and their limits.

Custom models and processes

Companion packages supply observation likelihoods and reuse tulpa’s inference and latent structures. tulpaObs provides models for occupancy, abundance, and detection; tulpaRatio provides models for ratios, rates, and proportions.

For a custom Gaussian latent process, supply its precision matrix and mean through R functions or a compiled C++ definition. The custom-process tutorial shows both interfaces. The EM + Laplace article describes the shared fitting framework for models with unobserved observation states.

Getting help

Questions and bug reports go to the GitHub issues. A bug report is easiest to act on with a small reproducible example, for instance made with reprex, and the output of sessionInfo().

Support

“Software is like sex: it’s better when it’s free.” — Linus Torvalds

I’m a PhD student who builds R packages in my free time because I believe good tools should be free and open. I started these projects for my own work and figured others might find them useful too.

If this package saved you some time, buying me a coffee is a nice way to say thanks. It helps with my coffee addiction.

<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tulpa>.
